A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiTCtrl and MPVBench. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments, MPVBench comparisons, a 28-participant user study, and component ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds transition visualizations and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: As specified in Section 3.3, latent blending changes from a two-segment mixture with complementary weights to a normalized weighted sum over overlapping segments. The weighting domain also changes from overlap length to segment length. This revises one inference component; the backbone and mask-guided KV-sharing remain intact. The PDFs do not establish whether implementation changes accompanied this revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 130-prompt MPVBench with ten transition types and retain single-prompt generation and video-editing applications. DAVIS is newly identified as the source of the existing natural-video reference in Figure 7, rather than establishing added dataset coverage. Additional t-SNE analyses reuse existing comparison cases.

E2.justification: v2 adds an Isolated comparator row to the qualitative comparisons in Figures 6, 18, and 19, corresponding to v1 Figures 6, 13, and 14. Although isolated generation already appeared in ablations, its participation in these comparisons is new. The comparator sets in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The main-text user-study description changes from a Likert scale to forced ranking, consistent with ranking instructions already present in v1's appendix; this does not establish a rerun. New Appendix G specifies timing comparisons for two and three prompts, targeting approximately 100 and 150 frames, with GPU-count exceptions explicitly recorded for Video-Infinity.

E4.justification: v2 adds t-SNE analyses of two retained qualitative cases in Figures 13–14, extending the investigation of transition continuity. Appendix G also analyzes runtime across prompt counts and with versus without masking. Existing component-ablation scores and mask-guidance case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both appendices report three random seeds for automatic evaluation. Neither version supplies new confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures for the comparisons.

E6.justification: Gen-L-Video's Table 1 CSCV, motion-smoothness, and text-image scores change from 59.44%, 83.36%, and 30.58% to 67.28%, 97.66%, and 30.60%; its Figure 6 outputs also change. v2 adds t-SNE results and timing results, including 5.3 minutes without masking versus approximately 39 minutes with masking for two prompts. DiTCtrl's principal benchmark scores and Tables 2 and 4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 5–6 substantively revise the mathematical blending definition: normalized aggregation replaces the complementary two-term mixture, and T denotes segment length instead of overlap length. This is more than a notation change. The attention-fusion and CSCV definitions remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The conclusion narrows MPVBench's novelty description from the 'first extensive evaluation framework' to a new benchmark with diverse transitions and specialized metrics. The principal claims about training-free MM-DiT generation, attention control, state-of-the-art performance, and computational efficiency are retained.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion explains the representative DAVIS reference and interprets additional t-SNE trajectories as resembling real-video continuity. Appendix G explicitly discusses the visual-quality/runtime tradeoff of masking and claims Pareto optimality despite its substantial overhead. The existing text-alignment tradeoff and stated limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Kling 1.5, Gen-L-Video's VideoCrafter2 backbone, matched baseline stride ratios, metric provenance, and additional timing/resource information. It also clarifies pairwise batched denoising. Most hyperparameters and the code URL were already supplied in v1; v2 drops the explicit pointer to an attached prompts.txt file without establishing that the resource itself was removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to MultiDiffusion, CLIPScore, VBench, and DAVIS, and removes the standalone ChatGPT reference while retaining GPT-4 attribution. Related work more explicitly credits earlier latent-blending approaches. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Section 4 is reorganized to separate benchmark description, quantitative evaluation, and human evaluation, and to reorder applications and ablations. The appendices separate implementation from evaluation details. Method explanations are condensed, and existing editing explanations are expanded in the main text, while most surrounding prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially reorganized: the teaser is redesigned, attention plots reformatted, the main ablation display condensed, and qualitative comparisons expanded. Existing editing examples are redisplayed in the main text; DAVIS frames, two t-SNE figures, and a timing table are added. Appendix galleries are extensively relocated, although many underlying examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the blending specification, reconciles the user-study terminology with the existing ranking instructions, and supplies useful baseline and metric details. Additional diagnostics and Table 5 make transition behavior and the substantial masking cost more assessable. These are limited but meaningful gains: the principal benchmark evidence and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged, and the broad efficiency claims are still insufficiently qualified.
